newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli cabinet approves competition measures.
newsitem.headline: Israeli cabinet approves competition measures.

text.p: Israel's cabinet on Wednesday approved most of a package of structural changes proposed by the Treasury to enhance competition in the economy.

"The (1997) budget cut was an essential measure but not sufficient," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said after what he described as an "historic" cabinet session. "Today we have begun to change things. We have opened to competition today the telecommunications market, transport and energy."
Netanyahu promised that by end of January he would unveil the government's long-awaited privatisation programme for 1997.

Of the 25 proposals for increasing competition and making the public sector more efficient, 17 were approved. Another eight, which the cabinet did not have time to vote on today, will be voted on at the regular weekly cabinet meeting on Friday.
Among the measures approved was to open public transport to competition, initially by allowing competition on three intercity routes.
The cabinet also voted in favour of plans for a tender to licence a third cellular telephone operator and to allow direct satellite television broadcasts.
The ministers also gave the go-ahead for further reforms in energy and to end the monopoly on agricultural exports now held by the state-owned Agrexco concern.

They also approved legislation that would prohibit the use of product standards to bar imports as well as a proposal to lower the port tax on imports and raise them on exports. They also approved forming a committee to weigh raising the official retirement age rom the current 65 for men and 60 for women.

"Our objectives are to accelerate growth, to increase the competitiveness of the economy, to moderate inflation and to make the various sectors of the economy more efficient," Finance Minister Dan Meridor said. "We are not concentrating on the (interests of) producers but on the consumers."

The cabinet approved all the major elements of the Treasury programme. Among the proposals it will take up on Friday are to step up tenders of state-owned lands and to do away with municipal tax exemptions on Friday.
Medridor said other structural reforms were in the pipeline, which are expected to include among other things electricity.
